dates.notes: Adopted by the OECD Council on 11 December 2019; the OECD Compendium records it as in force. It replaces the 2008 Recommendation on the Protection of Critical Information Infrastructures (OECD/LEGAL/0361). The official Compendium lists 39 adherents (38 OECD members and Brazil); the page does not print an explicit 'as of' date.

gaps: Non-binding: the Recommendation creates no treaty obligation, ratification, depositary, sanction or enforceable right.
The adherent list is maintained live in the OECD Compendium; the record is a snapshot at 24 November 2026, without a separate dated depositary table.
The list is essentially the OECD membership: 38 OECD members plus Brazil. It should not be read as an independent measure of global support for the Recommendation.
Only State adherents are recorded. The Recommendation is addressed to governments; implementation by private operators is a matter for adherents' domestic law.
The 2022 OECD digital-security package (OECD/LEGAL/0479-0482) is related but not merged into this record, because each recommendation has its own scope.
The full text is stored and segmented, but it was not read end-to-end for legal analysis in this acquisition pass.

languages.note: English and French are the OECD's official languages. Only the English page was read for this record.

legal_nature.rationale: An OECD Council Recommendation. It is a non-binding legal instrument: adherents accept political responsibility and report through OECD committees, but no treaty signature, ratification or enforcement follows.

endorsements.note: 39 named State adherents: 38 OECD members and Brazil. The OECD calls the list 'Adherents'; the count is reproduced from the official Compendium.

parties.summary: 39 States are listed as adherents: the 38 OECD members and Brazil, the only non-member adherent. Adherence is political, not a treaty signature or ratification. The list is essentially OECD membership plus one State and is not evidence of broader global support.
unknowns: The Compendium does not print a separate date for the current adherent count; the record uses the access date.
No public list of implementation measures by adherent is included here.

cyber_provisions: Section III — strategic approach: national objectives, governance and risk assessment for critical activities

Section V–VI — monitoring, supervision and integration into national risk management
Section VII — operator measures: governance, protection, detection and response, resilience
Section VIII–IX — partnerships and international cooperation
relevance.excluded_scope: A non-binding Recommendation addressed to States. It creates no treaty obligation, no depositary and no enforcement mechanism. The map records adherents, not signatures or ratifications. It is not a global supporter list: 38 of the 39 adherents are OECD members, and Brazil is the only non-member adherent.
relevance.reason: The OECD's current recommendation on the digital security of critical activities.
